sections.html: The first "Salminus" import of the year from the Orinoco river arrived, and all fish were Brycon hilarii. Luckily, pictures of Salminus of a similar size were taken last year, so a comparison is possible. On the internet many pictures are published under the name Salminus maxillosus that in fact show Brycon hilarii.
Basically a plant- and fruit-eating species, though it will eat very small fish.

Brycon hilarii is a comparatively peaceful fish. Of course it will not resist taking a very small fish as an appetizer, but basically it is a plant- and fruit-eating species. Among conspecifics it is very peaceful, in contrast to Salminus, which can be quite quarrelsome.

The correct scientific name of these imports is not easy to apply. In early 2017 a scientific revision of the genus Brycon was published. According to it there are four species of Brycon with a dark band in the caudal fin: B. orthotaenia, B. hilarii, B. whitei and B. polylepis. Of those, only the latter two occur naturally in the Orinoco, but both look totally different from these imports. B. whitei has a distinct dark band all over the body, and B. polylepis has a totally different body shape (much more slender than these fish). B. orthotaenia looks very much like these fish, but it is endemic to the Rio São Francisco. So the name Brycon hilarii is kept, although this species is recorded as occurring naturally only in the Amazon and Paraguay rivers, but it is bred and stocked as a food fish in many areas. Ongoing research may show that these fish belong to another species.
